item.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
item.description:
Tim’s view The breakdown of COP31 reveals a process in need of an overhaul, but the solution shouldn’t be hard to find. Depending on your perspective, the failure of negotiators in Türkiye to reach a consensus deal on transitioning away from fossil fuels may not actually be a failure. The UN process worked as designed: The minority of countries that wanted to avoid naming the root causes of climate change were blocked by the majority from pushing through a weak agreement. The compromises needed to achieve consensus in past COPs, the former UK climate advisor Michael Jacobs wrote this week , mainly served to dilute any sense of urgency; failure to reach an agreement is, in this telling, actually a stronger political signal about how deeply committed most countries are to decarbonization.
